title: How to become more patient, with Sarah Schnitker, PhD

sentences.en: Life is full of situations that try our patience.
sentences.zh: 生活中充满了考验我们耐心的时刻。

sentences.en: You're late for work and the driver in front of you is going 15 miles below the speed limit.
sentences.zh: 你上班迟到了，而前面的司机却以低于限速15英里的速度行驶。

sentences.en: Your preschooler insists on putting on her own shoes and it's taking 10 minutes per foot.
sentences.zh: 你的学龄前孩子坚持要自己穿鞋，每只脚都要花上10分钟。

sentences.en: You had an interview for your dream job weeks ago and you're waiting with increasing anxiety to hear back from the company.
sentences.zh: 几周前你参加了梦想工作的面试，现在正怀着越来越焦虑的心情等待公司的回复。

sentences.en: In each of these situations, you try to remain calm, but you can feel your stress level rising.
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，你努力保持冷静，但能感觉到自己的压力水平在上升。

sentences.en: Philosophers and religious leaders have long extolled the virtue of patience.
sentences.zh: 哲学家和宗教领袖长期以来一直赞美耐心的美德。

sentences.en: And in more recent years, psychologists have found that patience is good for our mental and even our physical health, but it's not easy to achieve.
sentences.zh: 近年来，心理学家发现耐心对我们的心理甚至生理健康都有好处，但要做到这一点并不容易。

sentences.en: So why is patience so hard to come by?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么耐心如此难得呢？

sentences.en: Has modern life and modern technology made us less patient?
sentences.zh: 现代生活和现代科技是否让我们变得更缺乏耐心了？

sentences.en: Is it possible to become a more patient person?
sentences.zh: 一个人有可能变得更有耐心吗？

sentences.en: And if you want to do so, what are the best strategies?
sentences.zh: 如果你想做到这一点，最好的策略是什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Sarah Schnitker, a professor of psychology and neuroscience at Baylor University, where she studies patience and other virtues, including self-control,
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是贝勒大学心理学和神经科学教授莎拉·施尼特克博士，她研究耐心和其他美德，包括自控力、

sentences.en: gratitude, and generosity.
sentences.zh: 感恩和慷慨。

sentences.en: She's especially interested in the role of spirituality and religion in virtue formation.
sentences.zh: 她对灵性和宗教在美德形成中的作用特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: Dr. Schnitker has published more than 100 peer-reviewed articles, and her work has been covered in mainstream media outlets, including The New York Times, CNN, and Time magazine.
sentences.zh: 施尼特克博士发表了100多篇同行评审文章，她的研究被《纽约时报》、CNN和《时代》杂志等主流媒体报道过。

sentences.en: Dr. Schnitker, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 施尼特克博士，感谢您今天参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to be here.
sentences.zh: 能来到这里真是太好了。

sentences.en: Most people know what the word patience means, but I'm curious how you define it in your work.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都知道“耐心”这个词的意思，但我很好奇您在工作中是如何定义它的。

sentences.en: Is it close to the way we think about it colloquially?
sentences.zh: 它和我们口语中理解的意思接近吗？

sentences.en: I think it is pretty similar.
sentences.zh: 我觉得非常相似。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think it's always interesting when we define the word to actually look at the Latin root.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我觉得当我们定义这个词时，去看看它的拉丁语词根总是很有趣的。

sentences.en: It actually means to suffer.
sentences.zh: 它实际上意味着“受苦”。

sentences.en: And so for many of us, when we have to be patient, we feel like we are suffering.
sentences.zh: 所以对我们许多人来说，当我们不得不保持耐心时，我们感觉自己是在受苦。

sentences.en: But the way we define it in psychology is that ability to remain calm and wait calmly in the face of frustration, adversity, or suffering.
sentences.zh: 但在心理学中，我们将其定义为在面对挫折、逆境或苦难时，保持冷静并从容等待的能力。

sentences.en: And so we all encounter people, events, kind of hardships in our daily lives that require us to wait and to put on the brakes a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都会在日常生活中遇到需要我们等待并稍微“踩刹车”的人、事件或困难。

sentences.en: And that can be really difficult.
sentences.zh: 这确实可能非常困难。

sentences.en: But if people who are patient are able to do that and still remain calm and settled and not become overwhelmed with emotion as they engage in that waiting.
sentences.zh: 但如果是有耐心的人，他们能够做到这一点，同时保持冷静和沉着，在等待的过程中不会被情绪所淹没。

sentences.en: Why is patience such a hard thing for some of us to achieve?
sentences.zh: 为什么耐心对我们中的一些人来说如此难以实现？

sentences.en: Or are we hardwired to be impatient?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们天生就缺乏耐心？

sentences.en: Well, that is a great question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I think, you know, patience, we are often employing patience in pursuit of our goals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，你知道，耐心，我们经常在追求目标的过程中运用耐心。

sentences.en: And we want to achieve either small goals of getting to work on time or big goals of raising a child who is a kind and generous person.
sentences.zh: 我们想要实现目标，无论是准时上班这样的小目标，还是培养一个善良慷慨的孩子这样的大目标。

sentences.en: And we often feel patient when we feel like something's blocking our goal pursuit and we want to get there faster.
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得有什么东西阻碍了我们的目标追求，而我们又想更快达到目标时，我们往往会感到缺乏耐心。

sentences.en: And so in some ways, we could say that impatience might have evolved evolutionarily to push us forward and make us notice when we need to move forward in our goals.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，我们可以说缺乏耐心可能是进化而来的，旨在推动我们前进，并让我们注意到何时需要推进我们的目标。

sentences.en: But oftentimes, it's useful to learn about what's going on from our emotions.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，了解我们的情绪所传达的信息是很有用的。

sentences.en: But then it's often not very helpful to kind of stay in this state of impatience and be overwhelmed with emotion.
sentences.zh: 然而，一直停留在这种缺乏耐心的状态并被情绪淹没，通常并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: And so having the capacity to regulate that impatience and be able to still pursue your goal, but in a more calm manner, it's really going to be kind of adaptive for us,
sentences.zh: 因此，拥有调节这种不耐烦的能力，并能够以更冷静的方式继续追求你的目标，这对我们来说确实是一种适应性的表现，

sentences.en: especially in the modern era where we aren't necessarily our goal for the day is not to find enough food so I can eat tonight.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在现代社会，我们当天的目标不一定是“找到足够的食物以便今晚能吃上饭”。

sentences.en: Some people deal with that, but many people kind of in Western industrialized context, right,
sentences.zh: 有些人确实面临这种情况，但许多处于西方工业化背景下的人，对吧，

sentences.en: that patience that maybe evolved for really life and death scenarios is being transferred over to other things that are not as life and death.
sentences.zh: 那种可能为真正的生死攸关场景而进化的耐心，正被转移到其他并非生死攸关的事情上。

sentences.en: And maybe we don't need as much of a strong inpatient reaction to.
sentences.zh: 也许我们不需要那么强烈的缺乏耐心的反应。

sentences.en: When do we first learn the concept of patience?
sentences.zh: 我们最初是在什么时候学会“耐心”这个概念的？

sentences.en: Did we discover the answer through Walter Mischel's famous marshmallow experiments?
sentences.zh: 我们是通过沃尔特·米歇尔著名的棉花糖实验发现答案的吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, we first learned, I mean, in psychology, I would say it really became popularized then.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我们最初学会，我的意思是，在心理学领域，我会说它确实是在那时开始普及的。

sentences.en: But the idea of patience is really an ancient concept.
sentences.zh: 但耐心的概念实际上是一个古老的概念。

sentences.en: And philosophers and theologians have been talking about patience for millennia and have recognized it as really a perennial human problem.
sentences.zh: 哲学家和神学家几千年来一直在谈论耐心，并将其视为一个永恒的人类问题。

sentences.en: But things do not go as fast as we want.
sentences.zh: 事情的发展并不总是如我们所愿那么快。

sentences.en: We are not able to kind of get past our suffering.
sentences.zh: 我们无法摆脱我们的苦难。

sentences.en: And so finding ways to wait and suffer with excellence is actually a thing a lot of philosophers talk about in virtue ethics.
sentences.zh: 因此，寻找以卓越的方式去等待和忍受的方法，实际上是许多哲学家在美德伦理学中讨论的话题。

sentences.en: And so it's been fun in psychology to come to this conversation a little bit later, but with our new methods of using scientific inquiry.
sentences.zh: 所以，心理学能稍晚一点加入这场对话，并运用我们科学探究的新方法，是一件很有趣的事情。

sentences.en: So just to reconstitute the question, is there an age in development that we learn, we begin to understand what patience is and how to exercise it?
sentences.zh: 那么，重新组织一下这个问题，在发育过程中，我们是在哪个年龄段开始理解什么是耐心以及如何运用它的？

sentences.en: We don't have for certain when patience itself develops, but we see immediately for an infant, they experience waiting, right?
sentences.zh: 我们并不确定耐心本身是在何时发展的，但我们能立即看到，婴儿就会经历等待，对吧？

sentences.en: That caregivers are not instantly responsive.
sentences.zh: 照顾者不会立即做出反应。

sentences.en: We try to be responsive when we're a caregiver.
sentences.zh: 作为照顾者，我们尽量做出回应。

sentences.en: But sometimes that baby has to wait for the bottle of milk to get warmed up.
sentences.zh: 但有时婴儿必须等待奶瓶热好。

sentences.en: But you see, when children start to get more of a theory of mind, kind of toddler years, they then start to maybe understand that they want something now.
sentences.zh: 但你会发现，当孩子开始具备更多的“心智理论”时，也就是幼儿时期，他们就开始明白自己想要某样东西。

sentences.en: Someone else doesn't want them to have that thing now, and they have to wait.
sentences.zh: 而别人不希望他们现在就得到那个东西，他们就必须等待。

sentences.en: And so you see in young children pretty early that they have impatience.
sentences.zh: 所以你在幼儿身上很早就看到了他们缺乏耐心。

sentences.en: They don't want to wait.
sentences.zh: 他们不想等待。

sentences.en: And any parent of a toddler can say, this is something I'm talking to them about regularly.
sentences.zh: 任何幼儿的父母都会说，这是我经常和他们谈论的事情。

sentences.en: And you're like, okay, good.
sentences.zh: 你会说，好吧，很好。

sentences.en: You get to practice your patience today.
sentences.zh: 你今天可以练习你的耐心了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We see that start to emerge.
sentences.zh: 我们看到这种特质开始显现。

sentences.en: But I think it's really in adolescence where people have this capacity to really intentionally cultivate the virtue of patience.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，真正能够有意识地培养耐心这种美德是在青春期。

sentences.en: And to think about kind of when is it wise to be patient?
sentences.zh: 去思考什么时候保持耐心是明智的？

sentences.en: When is it not wise?
sentences.zh: 什么时候是不明智的？

sentences.en: When should I actually allow myself to be upset if something appropriately to the situation?
sentences.zh: 如果事情确实令人不快，我什么时候应该允许自己适当地表达不满？

sentences.en: And so what we see start in early childhood kind of comes into full maturity in adolescence and young adulthood.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到在童年早期开始的东西，在青春期和成年早期走向了完全成熟。

sentences.en: In your work, you talk about three different kinds of patience, interpersonal, life hardship, and daily hassles.
sentences.zh: 在您的工作中，您谈到了三种不同的耐心：人际耐心、生活困境耐心和日常琐事耐心。

sentences.en: Tell us what each of those concepts mean.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我们这些概念分别意味着什么。

sentences.en: Interpersonal patience, as the name sounds, is about being patient with other people.
sentences.zh: 人际耐心，顾名思义，就是对他人保持耐心。

sentences.en: And I think this might not be the first thing that comes to mind for many people in the United States, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能不是美国许多人首先想到的，至少是这样。

sentences.en: We often think of patience, traffic, getting stuck in lines, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们通常想到耐心，会想到交通、排队等类似的事情。

sentences.en: But we actually find that interpersonal patience is quite important and predicts a lot of well-being outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但我们实际上发现人际耐心非常重要，并且预示着许多幸福的结果。

sentences.en: And I think this makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有道理。

sentences.en: If you're able to be patient with your spouse, you're going to have a better marriage and better health.
sentences.zh: 如果你能对你的配偶保持耐心，你就会拥有更好的婚姻和更健康的身体。

sentences.en: If, as a parent, you have to be patient with your child, as a co-worker, I have to be patient with the perhaps annoying person next to my office, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你作为父母，必须对孩子保持耐心；作为同事，我必须对办公室隔壁那个可能很烦人的人保持耐心，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, there's lots of people in our lives who are slower than we would like, who do things that we would prefer them not to do, and we have to practice our patience.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们生活中有很多比我们希望的要慢的人，他们做着我们希望他们不要做的事情，我们必须练习我们的耐心。

sentences.en: We also, with daily hassles patience, this might be the more stereotypic scenarios of getting stuck at a red light,
sentences.zh: 我们还有日常琐事耐心，这可能是更刻板的场景，比如被红灯卡住，

sentences.en: waiting on hold to change your airline ticket when it's canceled, right?
sentences.zh: 在航班取消时排队等待更改机票，对吧？

sentences.en: These things that are daily hassles that do test our patience as we wait, yet they're kind of smaller and build up across a day.
sentences.zh: 这些日常琐事确实在等待中考验我们的耐心，但它们比较琐碎，且在一天中不断累积。

sentences.en: And then the last type of patience, of life hardships patience, is kind of how we are patient with these very long-term goals that may or may not be resolved.
sentences.zh: 最后一种耐心，即生活困境耐心，是指我们如何对那些可能解决也可能无法解决的长期目标保持耐心。

sentences.en: So, for instance, if someone has a long-term chronic health condition, they may not actually think they'll get beat better or that it will improve,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果某人患有长期的慢性健康疾病，他们可能并不认为自己会好转或病情会改善，

sentences.en: but they still have to be patient as they deal with that chronic health condition across their life.
sentences.zh: 但他们在余生中应对这种慢性疾病时，仍然必须保持耐心。

sentences.en: And what does it mean to be able to wait?
sentences.zh: 能够等待意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, as you know it's going to be a very long time, you have to continue to engage this patience.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你知道的那样，这需要很长的时间，你必须持续地运用这种耐心。

sentences.en: And so, that could also include things of, like, dealing with an unjust society, dealing with the effects of systemic racism in your life, that it requires patience,
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能还包括应对不公正的社会、应对生活中系统性种族主义的影响等事情，这需要耐心，

sentences.en: but it's not something that you expect to have immediate end.
sentences.zh: 但这不是你期望能立即结束的事情。

sentences.en: And so, that adds another layer to that waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这为等待增加了一层含义。

sentences.en: Can you be good at patience in one of these domains, but not the others?
sentences.zh: 你能在其中一个领域擅长耐心，而在其他领域却不行吗？

sentences.en: For example, maybe you get crazed in traffic, but you can handle life's big challenges.
sentences.zh: 例如，也许你在交通堵塞时会抓狂，但你能处理生活中重大的挑战。

sentences.en: Is that the norm, or do the three types of patience generally correlate together?
sentences.zh: 这是常态，还是这三种耐心通常是相互关联的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we've seen variability.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我们已经看到了差异性。

sentences.en: So, when we look at these three types of patients, on average, they tend to correlate with each other.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们观察这三种耐心时，平均而言，它们往往是相互关联的。

sentences.en: So, and some of our research kind of has shown, too, that there might be this kind of general patience that influences kind of like you might have general intelligence,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的一些研究也表明，可能存在一种“一般耐心”，就像你可能拥有“一般智力”一样，

sentences.en: but then specific types of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 然后才是特定类型的智力。

sentences.en: We think that patience might be that way, that there's this kind of general emotion regulatory capacity to wait.
sentences.zh: 我们认为耐心可能也是这样，存在一种等待的通用情绪调节能力。

sentences.en: But there's distinctions in those different contexts of waiting.
sentences.zh: 但在不同的等待情境中存在区别。

sentences.en: And some people might really struggle with waiting with other people, but be okay with life hardships and things like that.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能在等待他人时非常挣扎，但在面对生活困境时却能应付自如。

sentences.en: And what we actually show in some of our studies, some of our studies, we actually do go more fine-grained and ask people about the goals they're pursuing in life.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们在一些研究中展示了这一点，我们确实做得更细致，询问人们他们正在追求的生活目标。

sentences.en: And they might say things like, be a good daughter, get straight A's, work out of the gym so many times a week.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会说，比如：做一个好女儿、拿到全A、每周去健身房锻炼几次。

sentences.en: And then we ask them for each of those individual goals, how much patience, items around how much patience they exert for that specific goal.
sentences.zh: 然后我们询问他们针对每一个个人目标，他们为该特定目标付出了多少耐心。

sentences.en: And what we found is there is a lot of variability.
sentences.zh: 我们发现存在很大的差异。

sentences.en: So, some people have a goal where they're very patient, and then they have a goal where they are not patient at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人对某个目标非常有耐心，但对另一个目标却完全没有耐心。

sentences.en: And, right, there's a lot of contextual features that might make that patience more or less difficult depending on the situation.
sentences.zh: 而且，确实，有很多情境特征可能会使耐心根据情况变得或多或少困难。

sentences.en: I get a lot of people, it's kind of funny, when I talk to people about patience, I can't tell you how many times people have talked about their golf game.
sentences.zh: 很多人，这很有趣，当我和人们谈论耐心时，我无法告诉你他们有多少次谈到了他们的高尔夫球比赛。

sentences.en: And how they are pretty good at patience, except when they're playing golf, and then they just cannot do it.
sentences.zh: 以及他们如何保持耐心，除了打高尔夫球的时候，那时他们就完全做不到了。

sentences.en: Or, like, people have lots of things in their lives that might be a particularly difficult circumstance.
sentences.zh: 或者，人们生活中有很多事情可能是一个特别困难的情况。

sentences.en: Or a game that really tests their patience.
sentences.zh: 或者是一个真正考验他们耐心的游戏。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask, you know, we talk about patience as a virtue, but is it always a virtue, or is it possible to be too patient?
sentences.zh: 那么请问，我们谈论耐心作为一种美德，但它总是美德吗？或者有可能过于耐心吗？

sentences.en: How do you judge when a situation requires patience and when it requires action, just in a way that anybody would agree?
sentences.zh: 你如何判断什么时候情况需要耐心，什么时候需要行动，以一种大家都同意的方式？

sentences.en: No, I think that's a great question, and actually really important.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这是一个很好的问题，而且实际上非常重要。

sentences.en: Because I think over the years, you know, sometimes patience is weaponized, and when someone wants someone else to be passive, they might say, well, you need to be patient.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为多年来，你知道，有时耐心被武器化了，当有人想让别人被动时，他们可能会说，嗯，你需要有耐心。

sentences.en: And in that case, it probably is not a virtue.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，它可能就不是一种美德了。

sentences.en: And so, I would argue that the capacity to wait calmly in the face of frustration and suffering, that capacity, the ability to do it as an individual, is a virtue, always.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在面对挫折和苦难时冷静等待的能力，这种能力，作为个人去做到这一点，永远是一种美德。

sentences.en: But whether or not exercising patience in a particular moment, part of the virtue is having the wisdom to know whether this is the right moment for patience,
sentences.zh: 但无论在特定时刻是否行使耐心，美德的一部分在于拥有智慧去判断这是否是保持耐心的正确时刻，

sentences.en: or for another capacity, or for another capacity, or virtue, like courage, for instance, which helps you act in the face of fear.
sentences.zh: 还是需要另一种能力，或者另一种美德，比如勇气，它能帮助你在面对恐惧时采取行动。

sentences.en: And so, we're using our patience in pursuit of goals.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在追求目标的过程中运用耐心。

sentences.en: Sometimes what's needed is to wait, and having the capacity to wait helps you be able to do that, if that is the wise thing to do.
sentences.zh: 有时需要的是等待，而拥有等待的能力有助于你在明智的情况下做到这一点。

sentences.en: But sometimes we also need to act, and take bold moves, and move forward.
sentences.zh: 但有时我们也需要行动，采取大胆的举措，向前迈进。

sentences.en: And I think the thing that patience as a virtue, kind of as this trait, this disposition that we have, is it gives you just enough space to remain calm,
sentences.zh: 我认为耐心作为一种美德，作为一种我们拥有的特质和倾向，它给了你足够的空间来保持冷静，

sentences.en: so you can decide if you're going to act or to wait.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以决定是采取行动还是等待。

sentences.en: Whereas, if you don't have that disposition and that capacity, that skill of patience, then you might just be buffeted around by your emotions.
sentences.zh: 而如果你没有那种倾向和能力，没有耐心这种技能，那么你可能就会被情绪所左右。

sentences.en: And so, an example I love to give is kind of, let's say, working against sexism in the workplace, for instance, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢举的一个例子是，比如，在职场中反对性别歧视，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, as a woman, sometimes I encounter a situation that involves sexism, and sometimes the wise thing to do is to speak up,
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一名女性，有时我会遇到涉及性别歧视的情况，有时明智的做法是站出来说话，

sentences.en: to pull upon my courage as a virtue in that capacity, and to do something.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻运用我作为美德的勇气，去做点什么。

sentences.en: Other times, it's not the right moment, and that actually being quiet and just remaining calm in this moment is the right thing to do, and I need my patience to help me do that.
sentences.zh: 而在其他时候，那不是正确的时机，保持安静并保持冷静实际上是正确的做法，我需要我的耐心来帮助我做到这一点。

sentences.en: And understanding, like, if my goal is to create an equitable, inclusive workplace, then I need to have both patience and courage to get me there.
sentences.zh: 并且明白，如果我的目标是创造一个公平、包容的工作场所，那么我需要同时具备耐心和勇气才能实现它。

sentences.en: And that way I can navigate situations well, and not just be driven by my anger, or by my fear, or by my, right?
sentences.zh: 这样我就可以很好地处理情况，而不是仅仅被我的愤怒、恐惧或我的……对吧？

sentences.en: That I have the capacity to regulate my emotions in a productive manner for the good of myself and others.
sentences.zh: 我有能力以一种对自己和他人都有益的生产性方式来调节我的情绪。

sentences.en: What do patience and impatience do to our bodies over the long term?
sentences.zh: 耐心和缺乏耐心从长远来看对我们的身体有什么影响？

sentences.en: There's a little bit of discussion out there of whether it's a discrete negative emotion different from other negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 目前有一些讨论，关于它是否是一种不同于其他负面情绪的离散负面情绪。

sentences.en: My colleague, Kate Sweeney, she argues that it is, and I think in a pretty convincing way.
sentences.zh: 我的同事凯特·斯威尼认为它是，而且我认为她的论点非常有说服力。

sentences.en: And inpatients, you know, we don't have research on it long term yet, because no one studied it discreetly, but we do know other negative emotions like anger, irritability.
sentences.zh: 至于缺乏耐心，你知道，我们还没有关于它的长期研究，因为没有人专门研究过它，但我们确实知道其他负面情绪，如愤怒、易怒。

sentences.en: These tax our system if we are feeling them consistently in daily life.
sentences.zh: 如果我们每天都在持续感受这些情绪，它们会损害我们的系统。

sentences.en: And so it can lead to cardiovascular problems, lead to a lot of chronic health conditions, roots in kind of persistent negative emotions in reaction to stress.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能导致心血管问题，导致许多慢性健康疾病，其根源在于对压力产生的持续负面情绪反应。

sentences.en: And so what we found is that when people are more patient, that might buffer against that,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，当人们更有耐心时，这可能会起到缓冲作用，

sentences.en: that they're able to regulate and be able to maintain their pursuit of the important goals in their life,
sentences.zh: 他们能够调节并保持对生活中重要目标的追求，

sentences.en: but not have the same cost physiologically as they have, they don't have as many negative emotions that are taxing them.
sentences.zh: 但生理上不会付出同样的代价，他们不会有那么多折磨他们的负面情绪。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下。

sentences.en: When we return, I'll talk to Dr. Schnitger about how to become more patient in your everyday life.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我将和施尼特克博士谈谈如何在日常生活中变得更有耐心。

sentences.en: So for people who want to become more patient, which is probably many of our listeners, what advice do you have?
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些想变得更有耐心的人，这可能是我们许多听众，你有什么建议？

sentences.en: What can you do to become more patient?
sentences.zh: 你能做些什么来变得更有耐心？

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I think people do want to become more patient, but they also don't want to become more patient.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们确实想变得更有耐心，但他们也不想变得更有耐心。

sentences.en: Because they're afraid that to become more patient, I'll have to practice patience, which means I'll have to wait and suffer and all these things.
sentences.zh: 因为他们担心如果变得更有耐心，我就必须练习耐心，这意味着我得等待、忍受痛苦以及经历所有这些事情。

sentences.en: I think I grew up in a religious community and like people would joke, but actually say seriously, like, don't pray for patience.
sentences.zh: 我想我是在一个宗教社区长大的，人们常会开玩笑，但其实是认真地说，比如，不要祈求耐心。

sentences.en: God will send you waiting and suffering.
sentences.zh: 上帝会让你经历等待和痛苦。

sentences.en: You don't want to pray for that.
sentences.zh: 你不会想祈求那个的。

sentences.en: It will mess up your life.
sentences.zh: 那会把你的生活搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: It's kind of interesting because we're told to be patient, but there's this real fear.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我们被教导要耐心，但内心却存在着真正的恐惧。

sentences.en: And so I think first understanding why it is you care about being patient is really important to motivate you.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，首先理解你为什么在乎耐心，对于激励自己非常重要。

sentences.en: So understanding if you're thinking about kind of your life in general, a particular situation.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论你是从整体生活还是特定情况来考虑，理解这一点都很重要。

sentences.en: So maybe I am struggling to be patient with my tween daughter and connecting to my big picture why of like,
sentences.zh: 也许我正在努力对我的青春期女儿保持耐心，并联系到我宏观的“为什么”，比如，

sentences.en: I view it as part of my job as a human being to like raise her to be a person of character in the world who contributes to society.
sentences.zh: 我将此视为我作为一个人职责的一部分，即把她培养成一个对世界有贡献、有品格的人。

sentences.en: And I view this even as a sacred activity that has immense meaning that when I think about that big picture purpose, then I can be motivated to say, okay,
sentences.zh: 我甚至认为这是一种具有巨大意义的神圣活动，当我想到那个宏大的目标时，我就能有动力对自己说，好吧，

sentences.en: what are practices that will help me be more patient in my interactions with her?
sentences.zh: 有哪些练习能帮助我在与她的互动中更有耐心？

sentences.en: And that's when you get into the how.
sentences.zh: 这就是你开始探讨“如何做”的时候。

sentences.en: So how do I learn to regulate my emotions with her?
sentences.zh: 那么，我该如何学习在与她相处时调节自己的情绪呢？

sentences.en: And right, we have a lot of strategies for emotion regulation that are evidence-based and all of these are really useful and can be applied to patients.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们有很多基于证据的情绪调节策略，所有这些都非常有用，并且可以应用于耐心培养。

sentences.en: So like one of the best strategies is cognitive reappraisal, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，最好的策略之一是认知重评，对吧？

sentences.en: So thinking about the situation in a new way.
sentences.zh: 也就是以一种新的方式思考当前的情况。

sentences.en: There's lots of ways to do cognitive reappraisal.
sentences.zh: 有很多方法可以进行认知重评。

sentences.en: It could be a perspective taking of like, okay, how would I feel if I were nine and didn't have control and had just been told this mean thing and right?
sentences.zh: 它可以是换位思考，比如，好吧，如果我九岁，没有控制权，刚被说了这句刻薄的话，我会是什么感觉？对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you know, kind of entering the other person's perspective can really help with interpersonal patients.
sentences.zh: 你知道，进入对方的视角真的有助于人际交往中的耐心。

sentences.en: We also find, I think, you know, with reappraising how long things take, taking a slight historical perspective can be very quick way to be patient.
sentences.zh: 我们还发现，我认为，你知道，通过重新评估事情所需的时间，采取一种稍微历史性的视角，可以成为保持耐心的一种非常快捷的方式。

sentences.en: So, you know, oh, why is this Wi-Fi so slow?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，哦，为什么这个Wi-Fi这么慢？

sentences.en: Like, actually, you know, just think about back to the 90s and you had dial-up and it had, like, you know, like just recalibrating our expectations through cognitive reappraisal.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你知道，回想一下90年代，那时你用的是拨号上网，它有，你知道，就像通过认知重评来重新校准我们的期望。

sentences.en: There's lots of ways we can change what we're thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过很多方式改变我们的想法。

sentences.en: But what we also kind of some research has found recently is that a variety of emotion regulation strategies can be helpful.
sentences.zh: 但我们也发现，最近的一些研究表明，多种情绪调节策略可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: So even distraction, even momentarily, sometimes suppression is the adaptive emotion regulation strategy in a particular moment.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是分心，哪怕是暂时的，有时压抑在特定时刻也是一种适应性的情绪调节策略。

sentences.en: And recent work that's come out has shown that it's actually having a variety of strategies in your tool belt for regulating your emotions that's really important and matching your strategy for patients to the situation.
sentences.zh: 最近的研究表明，在你的工具箱里拥有多种调节情绪的策略，并根据情况选择合适的耐心策略，这确实非常重要。

sentences.en: So sometimes it's like, you know what, I'm waiting on this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以有时就像，你知道吗，我正在等这件事。

sentences.en: I'm just going to distract myself with a TV show.
sentences.zh: 我打算看个电视节目来分散一下注意力。

sentences.en: Well, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: But other times, especially perhaps with scenarios that have kind of existential import,
sentences.zh: 但在其他时候，尤其是面对那些具有某种存在意义的情景时，

sentences.en: like a chronic health condition or dealing with injustice or things that are more those life hardships or with other people,
sentences.zh: 比如慢性健康状况、处理不公，或者那些生活中的艰辛，或者与他人相处时，

sentences.en: we might need more of that reappraisal to happen alongside.
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要更多的重评与这些情况同时进行。

sentences.en: It can't be the suppression or distraction, can't be the only strategy to work long term for being patient with those scenarios.
sentences.zh: 压抑或分心不能成为长期应对这些情景以保持耐心的唯一策略。

sentences.en: Sounds like some of this is to prevent yourself from ruminating on something that you have no control over.
sentences.zh: 听起来这其中一部分是为了防止你对自己无法控制的事情进行反刍。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's when patient and that's, I think, part of the reason patience is so hard for us in our cultural moment is, I mean, all humans like to have control and certainty.
sentences.zh: 这就是耐心，我认为这也是为什么在我们当下的文化中，耐心如此困难的部分原因，我的意思是，所有人类都喜欢拥有控制权和确定性。

sentences.en: But I think in the modern era, we have because of our technology,
sentences.zh: 但我认为在现代，因为我们的技术，

sentences.en: we have more illusions of control and have expectations of control that are just unrealistic for a human to have with our bodies or our minds and that we have to often just wait on things,
sentences.zh: 我们有了更多的控制幻觉，并且对控制权有着不切实际的期望，而人类在面对身体或思想时，往往不得不等待，

sentences.en: even though we think we shouldn't have to anymore.
sentences.zh: 即使我们认为我们不应该再等待了。

sentences.en: What if you have a spouse or a partner or even a kid whose patience meter is different from yours?
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个配偶、伴侣，甚至是一个孩子，他们的耐心程度和你不一样，该怎么办？

sentences.en: How do you deal with those situations where someone's losing it because they have to wait?
sentences.zh: 当有人因为不得不等待而崩溃时，你如何处理这些情况？

sentences.en: That's tough.
sentences.zh: 那很棘手。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard enough to be patient for yourself, but for someone else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对自己保持耐心已经够难了，更不用说对别人了。

sentences.en: But I think with other people, and especially you see this with children and adolescents, oftentimes you are co-regulating with them.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于其他人，尤其是你在儿童和青少年身上看到的，通常你是与他们共同调节情绪。

sentences.en: And even with a partner or spouse or co-worker, you can start to verbally do some of that reappraisal and think about things differently or help kind of start that regulation.
sentences.zh: 即使是与伴侣、配偶或同事，你也可以开始口头进行一些重评，以不同的方式思考问题，或者帮助开始那种调节。

sentences.en: So, for example, you know, amusement parks, I think, are like an experiment in patience.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，你知道，游乐园，我认为就像是一个关于耐心的实验。

sentences.en: I want to do a study at one someday.
sentences.zh: 我希望有一天能在那里做一项研究。

sentences.en: Waiting in line.
sentences.zh: 排队等待。

sentences.en: Waiting in line.
sentences.zh: 排队等待。

sentences.en: For 10 seconds of fear.
sentences.zh: 为了10秒钟的惊险。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: What are we doing to ourselves?
sentences.zh: 我们对自己做了什么？

sentences.en: But it's interesting to see like what people do like with their children or with their partners as they do that.
sentences.zh: 但观察人们在做这些事时如何对待孩子或伴侣，这很有趣。

sentences.en: And, right, do you get to talk about other things?
sentences.zh: 而且，对吧，你们会聊些别的事情吗？

sentences.en: Do you distract them?
sentences.zh: 你会分散他们的注意力吗？

sentences.en: Do you say, OK, you know, at least it's better than that other ride that had the two hour wait, right?
sentences.zh: 你会说，好吧，你知道，至少这比那个要等两个小时的游乐设施好，对吧？

sentences.en: You can really start to see how strategies are used socially.
sentences.zh: 你真的可以开始看到策略是如何在社交中被使用的。

sentences.en: And I think we can do that in our own lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以在自己的生活中做到这一点。

sentences.en: And you have to be careful when you're helping someone else,
sentences.zh: 而且你在帮助别人时必须小心，

sentences.en: because what might be a strategy that works for you or what feels like the wise thing to do for you might not be the same for them.
sentences.zh: 因为对你有效的策略，或者你认为明智的做法，对他们来说可能并不适用。

sentences.en: So, for example, I mentioned Kate Sweeney earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，我之前提到的凯特·斯威尼（Kate Sweeney）。

sentences.en: She's done studies in the past on women waiting for breast biopsy results to find out if they have cancer.
sentences.zh: 她过去曾对等待乳房活检结果以确定是否患癌的女性进行过研究。

sentences.en: These other kind of really uncertain waiting scenarios.
sentences.zh: 这些是其他那种非常不确定的等待情景。

sentences.en: And you want to make sure that the support a partner provides is actually supportive and not kind of out of step with what the individual needs.
sentences.zh: 你需要确保伴侣提供的支持确实是支持性的，而不是与个人需求脱节的。

sentences.en: And so I think it's always wise to also be checking in, especially if it's another adult you're waiting alongside to see what they need.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，尤其是当你与另一位成年人一起等待时，随时询问他们需要什么总是明智的。

sentences.en: And would it be helpful to go distract ourselves right now?
sentences.zh: 现在分散一下注意力会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to talk it through?
sentences.zh: 你想谈谈吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to engage in problem solving?
sentences.zh: 你想一起解决问题吗？

sentences.en: Like, we always often forget we can just ask other people how we can help them.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们总是经常忘记我们可以直接问别人我们能如何帮助他们。

sentences.en: And I think that's a really wise step and lets the person get the kind of support they need.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常明智的步骤，能让对方得到他们需要的支持。

sentences.en: Now, I'm originally from New York, and I can attest to the fact that New Yorkers are notoriously impatient.
sentences.zh: 现在，我来自纽约，我可以证明纽约人以没耐心著称。

sentences.en: Tourists work too slowly, out-of-towners don't know how to drive.
sentences.zh: 游客动作太慢，外地人不会开车。

sentences.en: And whenever I go back to New York, I get into that mindset.
sentences.zh: 每当我回到纽约，我就会进入那种心态。

sentences.en: So I need to ask, is impatience contagious?
sentences.zh: 所以我需要问，没耐心会传染吗？

sentences.en: Is it cultural?
sentences.zh: 这是文化使然吗？

sentences.en: You know, I don't have actual hard data on this yet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我还没有这方面的确凿数据。

sentences.en: But, I mean, we know there's emotion contagion for other emotions, and we've clearly seen that.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，我们知道其他情绪存在情绪传染，我们已经清楚地看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I would hypothesize that it is contagious.
sentences.zh: 我会假设它是会传染的。

sentences.en: And that when we see other people around us, especially if we're experiencing some arousal, but haven't quite decided what we're feeling yet,
sentences.zh: 当我们看到周围的人，特别是如果我们正经历某种兴奋，但还没完全决定自己感受如何时，

sentences.en: if we see someone else there tapping their fingers, fidgeting, showing all those signs of impatience, we can catch it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看到别人在那里敲手指、坐立不安，表现出所有那些没耐心的迹象，我们就会被传染。

sentences.en: And that's concerning, right?
sentences.zh: 这很令人担忧，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we can create whole communities of impatience.
sentences.zh: 因为我们可以创造出整个没耐心的社区。

sentences.en: I think culture specifically comes into play in the fact that culture sets our expectations of how life should go.
sentences.zh: 我认为文化在其中发挥了作用，因为文化设定了我们对生活应该如何发展的期望。

sentences.en: And I think when I think of comparing New York to, say, Texas, where I live currently.
sentences.zh: 当我想到将纽约与我目前居住的德克萨斯州进行比较时。

sentences.en: When I moved to Texas, I lived in L.A.
sentences.zh: 当我搬到德克萨斯州时，我之前住在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: before that.
sentences.zh: 在那之前。

sentences.en: It was one of the things that most struck me with this culture shift was things were slower in Texas.
sentences.zh: 这是最让我感到文化冲击的事情之一，德克萨斯州的事情节奏更慢。

sentences.en: And that everyone wanted to chat more.
sentences.zh: 而且每个人都更愿意聊天。

sentences.en: And part of it, I think, is, right, the crowd.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因是，对吧，人群。

sentences.en: The crowd is making you want to get through faster.
sentences.zh: 人群让你想要更快地通过。

sentences.en: But, right, there's just a different culture of taking time.
sentences.zh: 但是，对吧，这里有一种不同的“花时间”的文化。

sentences.en: And the expectation of how long it should take to go through the checkout line is just different because of what that culture values.
sentences.zh: 而且因为该文化所重视的东西，对结账排队需要多长时间的期望就是不同。

sentences.en: And, right, in kind of the South, you have more relational cultures.
sentences.zh: 而且，对吧，在南方，你有更多的人际关系文化。

sentences.en: Southern hospitality, right?
sentences.zh: 南方好客，对吧？

sentences.en: You see that those values show up in our approach to time and what is time.
sentences.zh: 你看到这些价值观体现在我们对待时间的方式以及什么是时间上。

sentences.en: And I think maybe a place like New York City, right, our metaphor of time is that time is money, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为也许像纽约市这样的地方，对吧，我们对时间的隐喻是时间就是金钱，对吧？

sentences.en: It's all around the stock market and Wall Street and, right, that this is how we think about time.
sentences.zh: 它围绕着股票市场和华尔街，对吧，这就是我们思考时间的方式。

sentences.en: But our views of time definitely differ across culture significantly, not just in the U.S., but around the world.
sentences.zh: 但我们对时间的看法在不同文化中确实存在显著差异，不仅是在美国，在世界各地也是如此。

sentences.en: Really different views of time.
sentences.zh: 非常不同的时间观。

sentences.en: Is it linear?
sentences.zh: 它是线性的吗？

sentences.en: Is it circular?
sentences.zh: 它是循环的吗？

sentences.en: Do we go by clock time or event time?
sentences.zh: 我们是按时钟时间还是事件时间来生活？

sentences.en: That the time something's supposed to start is once everyone arrives?
sentences.zh: 即某事应该开始的时间是每个人都到达的时候？

sentences.en: Like, these are just fundamentally different views of time that are going to shape when we think too much time has passed and triggers that impatience.
sentences.zh: 这些是根本不同的时间观，它们会影响我们认为什么时候时间过得太久，并触发那种没耐心。

sentences.en: I've seen meditation or mindfulness mentioned as strategies to increase patience.
sentences.zh: 我看到冥想或正念被提及作为增加耐心的策略。

sentences.en: Do those work?
sentences.zh: 那些有效吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Those are effective for increasing patience.
sentences.zh: 那些对于增加耐心是有效的。

sentences.en: And I think part of the reason, right, we know that meditation helps you calm your own physiological system, calm your mind.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因是，对吧，我们知道冥想能帮助你平静自己的生理系统，平静你的思想。

sentences.en: And so just having the capacity to calm yourself, even through a very brief meditative practice, is really a great tool for regulation.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使通过非常简短的冥想练习，拥有平静自己的能力，也是调节情绪的绝佳工具。

sentences.en: You know, meditation also, and it's focused on especially mindfulness with non-judgment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，冥想也专注于非评判的正念。

sentences.en: It might allow us to sit in these moments where we're waiting with less judgment of it and more of a sense of, ah, this is just something that is.
sentences.zh: 它可能让我们坐在这些等待的时刻，减少对它的评判，更多地感受到，啊，这只是一件正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And something, instead of waiting seen as something I have to, like, endure and suffer,
sentences.zh: 而不是把等待看作是我必须忍受和痛苦的事情，

sentences.en: see as this is just the experience of waiting and this is part of being human can kind of shift.
sentences.zh: 将其视为这就是等待的体验，这是作为人类的一部分，可以产生某种转变。

sentences.en: It's a minor shift, but can really help as we deal with that component of life.
sentences.zh: 这是一个微小的转变，但在我们处理生活的这一部分时真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: What got you interested in studying patience?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你对研究耐心感兴趣？

sentences.en: I started studying as a first-year grad student and positive psychology and the study of character strengths and virtues was just kind of blossoming in 2004.
sentences.zh: 我是在读研究生一年级时开始研究的，积极心理学以及对性格优势和美德的研究在2004年刚刚兴起。

sentences.en: And as I was looking at the literature, it just struck me that all the virtues that were being studied had a very push-through, goal-directed, power-through-it, happy flavor.
sentences.zh: 当我查阅文献时，我发现所有被研究的美德都有一种非常“冲刺”、以目标为导向、克服困难、快乐的色彩。

sentences.en: And I noticed that patience was completely neglected.
sentences.zh: 我注意到耐心完全被忽视了。

sentences.en: And it was excluded, for instance, from Seligman and Peterson's 24 virtues they had in their values and action inventory.
sentences.zh: 例如，它被排除在塞利格曼（Seligman）和彼得森（Peterson）在他们的价值观和行动清单中的24种美德之外。

sentences.en: And I read this book.
sentences.zh: 我读了这本书。

sentences.en: It was actually an interdisciplinary reading.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一次跨学科阅读。

sentences.en: I do a lot of collaboration with philosophers and theologians.
sentences.zh: 我与哲学家和神学家有很多合作。

sentences.en: And I read a book by a moral philosopher, David Bailey-Harned, argued that since the Industrial Revolution, patience has gone out of fashion,
sentences.zh: 我读了一位道德哲学家大卫·贝利-哈内德（David Bailey-Harned）的书，他认为自工业革命以来，耐心已经过时了，

sentences.en: that we have abandoned it as a capacity we want to cultivate in ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们已经放弃了它作为我们想要在自己身上培养的一种能力。

sentences.en: Because we think the solution to waiting is technological instead of human, that we think any time we have to wait or suffer, there's a quick fix, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我们认为等待的解决方案是技术的而不是人类的，我们认为任何时候我们必须等待或受苦，都有一个快速的解决方法，对吧？

sentences.en: We should fix it through our technology instead of recognizing that this is a deeply human concern.
sentences.zh: 我们应该通过我们的技术来解决它，而不是认识到这是一个深刻的人类问题。

sentences.en: And that really was very compelling to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说真的非常有说服力。

sentences.en: Because if you think about the things that give meaning to life and are most important, they always do take time.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你思考那些赋予生活意义且最重要的事情，它们总是需要时间。

sentences.en: And there's not a technological solution to learning to wait for my spouse to grow in the way he's going to grow and not the way I want him to be, right?
sentences.zh: 对于学习等待我的配偶以他自己的方式成长，而不是以我想要他成为的方式成长，并没有技术解决方案，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not...
sentences.zh: 它们不是……

sentences.en: Our human problems require patience.
sentences.zh: 我们的人类问题需要耐心。

sentences.en: And so I just thought, oh, my goodness, this is a real problem that we're not talking about this.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想，天哪，这是一个我们没有讨论的真正问题。

sentences.en: And we're going to be unprepared when it comes to moments where we really have to wait.
sentences.zh: 当我们真正需要等待的时刻到来时，我们将毫无准备。

sentences.en: And I think people often do feel unprepared in those moments of deep waiting, of waiting for net breast biopsy result, or waiting for these things.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们在那些深度等待的时刻，在等待乳房活检结果，或等待这些事情时，确实经常感到毫无准备。

sentences.en: We have to practice it in the small things so that we can be ready to do it in the larger things.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在小事中练习它，这样我们才能准备好在更大的事情中做到这一点。

sentences.en: And it's interesting to time it to the Industrial Revolution, because if you think about before that, what people were doing was farming,
sentences.zh: 将其与工业革命联系起来很有趣，因为如果你想想在那之前，人们做的是农业，

sentences.en: which requires a lot of patience and waiting and plant a seed.
sentences.zh: 这需要大量的耐心和等待，种下一颗种子。

sentences.en: It's going to be months and months before you see a crop.
sentences.zh: 你要等上好几个月才能看到庄稼。

sentences.en: So that makes a whole lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有道理。

sentences.en: Some of our modern societies, we've lost a sense of these rhythms of life.
sentences.zh: 在我们的一些现代社会中，我们已经失去了对这些生活节奏的感觉。

sentences.en: Life of, right, there's a planting seed, right?
sentences.zh: 生活，对吧，有播种，对吧？

sentences.en: Those rhythms that you have if you're more connected to the natural environment.
sentences.zh: 如果你与自然环境联系更紧密，你就会拥有那些节奏。

sentences.en: And so I think we maybe suffer a bit more as humans when we get disconnected from the natural world.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为当我们与自然世界脱节时，作为人类，我们可能会遭受更多的痛苦。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of research showing that.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多研究表明这一点。

sentences.en: So I think that's one of the reasons is the wisdom of timing and waiting that we need to maintain.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是我们需要保持的时间和等待的智慧的原因之一。

sentences.en: So just to wrap up, what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么最后，你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are your big questions that you're trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 你试图回答的核心问题是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I have a, actually next month, we start data collection, looking at patients and parents of adolescents.
sentences.zh: 是这样，下个月我们就要开始收集数据了，研究对象是青少年及其父母。

sentences.en: It's going to be a four-year longitudinal study where we look at not just kind of their self-reports, but also how other people in their lives think they are or are not patient.
sentences.zh: 这将是一项为期四年的纵向研究，我们不仅会观察他们的自我报告，还会观察他们生活中其他人认为他们是否有耐心。

sentences.en: We'll also do psychophysio measurement in the lab and do experience sampling.
sentences.zh: 我们还会在实验室进行心理生理测量，并进行体验取样。

sentences.en: So ping them multiple times.
sentences.zh: 也就是多次给他们发送提醒。

sentences.en: It's going to be a really holistic view of these parents.
sentences.zh: 这将是对这些父母非常全面的观察。

sentences.en: And we chose to look at parents of adolescents because they are a very stressed group.
sentences.zh: 我们选择研究青少年的父母，因为他们是一个压力非常大的群体。

sentences.en: When you look at parenting, I mean, everyone, when they think of patients, think of parenting, anyone who's been a parent.
sentences.zh: 谈到育儿，我想每个人，只要当过父母的人，在想到耐心时，都会想到育儿。

sentences.en: But parents of adolescents actually show the lowest parental satisfaction and very, very high rates of stress.
sentences.zh: 但青少年的父母实际上表现出的育儿满意度最低，压力水平也非常非常高。

sentences.en: Because part of what you're doing there is you have less and less control, more risks to your child as well as you give out that control and have to wait for them kind of to grow.
sentences.zh: 因为你所做的一部分工作是，你对孩子的控制力越来越小，而随着你放手并等待他们成长，孩子面临的风险也随之增加。

sentences.en: And so we wanted to look at, and we're looking at patients in adversity in particular.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想研究，而且我们特别关注处于逆境中的父母的耐心。

sentences.en: So looking at parents of adolescents who face particular challenges or adversities in their lives that might make patients particularly important.
sentences.zh: 也就是观察那些在生活中面临特殊挑战或逆境的青少年父母，在这些情况下，耐心可能尤为重要。

sentences.en: So, for example, we're studying parents of adolescents with developmental disabilities to see how not only they're patient with their child,
sentences.zh: 例如，我们正在研究有发育障碍青少年的父母，看看他们不仅是对孩子有耐心，

sentences.en: but with all the health care systems they have to navigate and the school systems and ensuring that their child is taken care of.
sentences.zh: 还要应对他们必须接触的所有医疗系统和学校系统，以确保他们的孩子得到照顾。

sentences.en: We're also examining patients among Muslim American parents and the unique stressors they face around maintaining their culture and their faith tradition in a context in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们还在研究美国穆斯林父母的耐心，以及他们在维持自身文化和信仰传统时所面临的独特压力，特别是在美国这样的环境中，

sentences.en: that is not always friendly to their culture or faith or tradition and how they negotiate parenting in that context and being patient, but yet acting with courage when necessary.
sentences.zh: 这里并不总是对他们的文化、信仰或传统友好，我们研究他们如何在这样的背景下进行育儿，既保持耐心，又能在必要时勇敢行动。

sentences.en: We're also looking at a sample of parents in Southern California who are really ethnically,
sentences.zh: 我们还在南加州选取了一个样本，那里的父母在种族和

sentences.en: socioeconomically diverse and looking at how those different components of their societal location affect their patients across time and their well-being.
sentences.zh: 社会经济地位上非常多样化，我们研究这些社会地位的不同组成部分如何随时间影响他们的耐心和幸福感。

sentences.en: So I'm really excited to dig into this particular population.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常期待深入研究这个特定群体。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, that sounds like great stuff.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常棒。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Schnicker, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 那么，Schnicker博士，感谢您今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed our conversation.
sentences.zh: 我很享受我们的谈话。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org，或者在Apple、Spotify、YouTube以及任何您获取播客的地方收听《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave a review.
sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢我们的节目，请订阅并留下评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future episodes, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的节目有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由Lee Weinerman制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是Kim Mills。
